evidence.claim: The Prime Minister is the chief executive, chair of the Council of Ministers, commander-in-chief of the national armed forces, and responsible to the House of Peoples’ Representatives.
evidence.title: Constitution of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
evidence.excerpt: The Prime Minister is the chief executive, chair of the Council of Ministers, commander-in-chief of the national armed forces, and responsible to the House of Peoples’ Representatives.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text hosted by WIPO Lex; stable de jure authority and constraint rules.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for Abiy’s office and formal authority, but not a 2022 action record.
contrary_evidence: De jure authority does not itself show any nuclear or existential-risk decision in 2022.

evidence.claim: The African Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zone Treaty prohibits research, development, manufacture, stockpiling, acquisition, testing, possession, control, or stationing of nuclear weapons, and Ethiopia is listed among the African States that have signed it.
evidence.title: Treaty of Pelindaba
evidence.publisher: United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs
evidence.excerpt: The African Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zone Treaty prohibits research, development, manufacture, stockpiling, acquisition, testing, possession, control, or stationing of nuclear weapons, and Ethiopia is listed among the African States that have signed it.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN disarmament overview of the treaty and African signatories.
evidence.period_fit: Stable regional legal posture applicable in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Inherited treaty constraint on Ethiopia; not a ruler-specific initiative in 2022.
contrary_evidence: The overview does not say how Ethiopia implemented the treaty in 2022.
Signature status alone does not prove day-to-day compliance.

evidence.claim: Ethiopia has an in-force IAEA safeguards agreement under the NPT and an Additional Protocol signature recorded in 2019.
evidence.title: Country List: Ethiopia, Federal Democratic Republic of
evidence.excerpt: Ethiopia has an in-force IAEA safeguards agreement under the NPT and an Additional Protocol signature recorded in 2019.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IAEA legal factsheet listing safeguards instruments and status.
evidence.period_fit: Current status that reflects a long-running safeguards framework relevant to 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level nuclear-safety and verification baseline; not Abiy-personal conduct.
contrary_evidence: Current page rather than a 2022 snapshot.
Does not demonstrate how much authority Abiy personally exercised over these files.

evidence.claim: Ethiopia’s IAEA cooperation priorities included energy planning, environmental protection, and radiation safety, security, and waste management, alongside health, agriculture, and water.
evidence.title: Ethiopia signs its third Country Programme Framework (CPF) for 2012-2017
evidence.excerpt: Ethiopia’s IAEA cooperation priorities included energy planning, environmental protection, and radiation safety, security, and waste management, alongside health, agriculture, and water.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IAEA description of Ethiopia’s peaceful nuclear technical-cooperation priorities.
evidence.period_fit: Historical but relevant as the longstanding peaceful-use template that framed 2022.
contrary_evidence: This is a 2012 framework, not a 2022 action.
It speaks to peaceful nuclear capacity-building, not nuclear-risk decisions.

evidence.claim: SIPRI identifies only nine nuclear-armed states worldwide, and Ethiopia is not among them.
evidence.title: 6. World nuclear forces
evidence.excerpt: SIPRI identifies only nine nuclear-armed states worldwide, and Ethiopia is not among them.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Leading research institute’s global nuclear-forces overview; strong for structural context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a country-exposure constraint, not an Abiy action.
contrary_evidence: The source does not address Ethiopia’s internal emergency, dual-use, or cyber/biological risk choices.
It is a global status list, so the inference that Ethiopia had no nuclear-weapon authority is indirect.
